raw_response:
I have been farming this same piece of land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My father grew wheat and corn here, and I grow wheat and corn here. I don't have money to gamble on something new, and at 73 my body won't let me take risks. The wheat-corn rotation is what I know. That is what I will grow.

My plot is about 6 mu. My son is in Shijiazhuang now, so most of the work falls to me. I have to be realistic about what I can manage.

For wheat, I already planted Kenong 199 last October — it stands up well and the village seed shop always has it. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, then I top-dress with urea when the plants start jointing in spring. I water four times: once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once at heading, and once when the grain is filling. Wheat needs water or the yield drops badly. I spray herbicide early, then I watch for aphids and powdery mildew in May — those I spray too if I see them. I always rotary-till before planting in October.

For corn, I will plant Zhengdan 958 in June right after wheat harvest. Everyone uses it. I do a light rotary pass on the stubble, broadcast compound fertilizer, and top-dress urea at big bell stage. Summer rains usually come, but I pump from the well twice just to make sure — once at germination if it's dry, once at silking. I spray herbicide right after planting and watch for corn borer. The corn takes care of itself more than the wheat does.

I expect about 450 jin per mu on wheat, maybe 550 on corn. Nothing special, but enough to cover costs and feed ourselves.
